terms.comment: Mostly in the ablative: mōmentō temporis, in a moment (see in a moment); hōrae mōmentō, in the space of an hour.

evidence: Cic. Sest. 53: pūnctō temporis eōdem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: nē pūnctum quidem temporis, not for a moment (Cic. Phil. 8.20, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: for a moment, for a little while
evidence: Traupman 87: wait a minute, manē paulisper

phrases.latin: sapientis quoque animum paulisper movērī et contrahī et pallēscere necessum est
phrases.english: even a wise man’s mind is bound to be shaken for a moment, to shrink and to turn pale

sources: Lewis & Short: momentum · Lewis & Short: punctum · Lewis & Short: paulisper
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 87, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.
